title: Fewer Americans use cash today than a decade ago, but many still carry it
summary: Today, 42% of U.S. adults say they don’t use cash for any purchases in a typical week. This is up from 24% in 2015.

title: Americans want transparency when AI is used in their healthcare
summary: About seven-in-ten U.S. adults (72%) say it’s extremely or very important that a doctor or other healthcare provider tells them if they’re using AI in their healthcare.

title: From Diagnoses to Treatments, Why Americans Use AI Chatbots for Health
summary: Americans use chatbots for a host of health-related reasons, from helping make diagnoses on their own to learning more about information they may have gotten from a doctor. Nearly all chatbot health users find this AI information helpful.

title: Do Americans think chatbots help or hurt people using them for loneliness, depression or stress?
summary: Key takeaways: At a time of public debate and high-profile cases of chatbot use for social and mental health, a new Pew Research Center survey finds that, on balance, Americans say chatbots do more to hurt than help people who use them for loneliness, depression or stress. title: How South Koreans view their relationship with the U.S.
summary: For the first time in over 20 years, a majority of South Koreans have an unfavorable opinion of the U.S.

title: How Much of the Internet Is Written With AI?
summary: In a random sample of 10,000 webpages collected in July 2026, one-in-ten show signs of being written or substantially edited by AI.

title: Is teen summer employment in the U.S. rebounding after a long fade?
summary: Only 35.5% of U.S. teens ages 16 to 19 worked this summer, up slightly from 2025 but far below the more than half who worked most summers before 2000.

title: Young adults in the U.S. are increasingly wary of AI, concerned it will take jobs
summary: About half of Americans say they're more concerned than excited about AI, and young adults' concern is rising.

title: Refugee admissions to the U.S. are dropping sharply in Trump’s second term
summary: U.S. refugee admissions have dropped sharply in Trump's second term, with just over 10,000 so far in fiscal 2026, down from about 38,000 in fiscal 2025.

title: Americans’ use of social media for health information differs by race and ethnicity
summary: Hispanic, Black, and Asian adults are more likely than White adults to get health information from social media and turn to health and wellness influencers.

title: India and Pakistan: Rivals With Divergent Views of the Global Order
summary: Indians and Pakistanis tend to name the other country as their top threat, and each side doubts the other's commitment to good relations.

title: How do South Asians view other countries in the region?
summary: We asked adults in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka how they view other South Asian countries. Only Sri Lanka receives more positive than negative ratings from the other three publics.

title: Second Trump administration has ended Temporary Protected Status for most immigrants who had it
summary: The second Trump administration has ended Temporary Protected Status for 13 countries, affecting roughly 1 million recipients.

title: Most U.S. adults have lived with a romantic partner they’re not married to by their early 40s
summary: Around three-quarters of Americans in their late 30s or early 40s have lived with a romantic partner they’re not married to at some point in their lives.

title: Most Americans are uncomfortable with transgender athletes on sports teams that don’t match their birth sex
summary: Most Americans are not comfortable with transgender athletes competing on teams that don't match their birth sex.
